answer: Property foreclosed for delinquent taxes is sold at auction by the foreclosing governmental unit (or its authorized agent) at one or more sales, which may include an online auction.
quote: the foreclosing governmental unit, or its authorized agent, at the option of the foreclosing governmental unit, shall hold 1 or more property sales at 1 or more convenient locations at which property foreclosed by a judgment entered under section 78k will be sold by auction sale, which may include an auction sale conducted via an internet website.
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature

answer: Sales are held between the third Tuesday in July after the foreclosure judgment and the following first Tuesday in November.
quote: beginning on the third Tuesday in July immediately succeeding the entry of the judgment under section 78k vesting absolute title to tax delinquent property in the foreclosing governmental unit and ending on the immediately succeeding first Tuesday in November, the foreclosing governmental unit, or its authorized agent, at the option of the foreclosing governmental unit, shall hold 1 or more property sales
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature

answer: Sales are held at one or more convenient locations and may include an auction conducted via an internet website.
quote: shall hold 1 or more property sales at 1 or more convenient locations at which property foreclosed by a judgment entered under section 78k will be sold by auction sale, which may include an auction sale conducted via an internet website.
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
Foreclosing Governmental Units List
note: No statewide registration rule was found; registration is set by each county or its sale platform.

source_title: Foreclosing Governmental Units List
note: The statute does not set a deposit; check the county or its sale platform.

answer: The minimum bid must include all delinquent taxes, interest, penalties and fees on the property, and may include the foreclosing governmental unit's additional expenses for forfeiture, foreclosure, maintenance, repair or remediation.
quote: The minimum bid must include all of the delinquent taxes, interest, penalties, and fees due on the property, and may include any additional expenses incurred by the foreclosing governmental unit in connection with the forfeiture, foreclosure, maintenance, repair, or remediation of the property
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
note: At the final sale the minimum bid is not required; the county may set a reasonable opening bid to recover sale costs (MCL 211.78m(5)).

answer: The county must require full payment at the close of each day's bidding or by a date no more than 21 days after the sale.
quote: The foreclosing governmental unit shall require full payment at the close of each day's bidding or by a date not more than 21 days after the sale.
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature

answer: Before the property is conveyed, the buyer must give the county proof of paying the local tax collecting unit any property taxes owed on the property at the time of the sale.
quote: Before the foreclosing governmental unit conveys a property sold at a sale, the purchaser shall provide the foreclosing governmental unit with proof of payment to the local tax collecting unit in which the property is located of any property taxes owed on the property at the time of the sale.
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
note: MCL 211.78m(10): 'The foreclosing governmental unit may charge a fee in excess of the minimum bid and any sale proceeds for the cost of recording a deed under this subsection.'

answer: All redemption rights expire on the March 31 after the foreclosure judgment is entered, or 21 days after the judgment in a contested case.
quote: All redemption rights to the property expire on the March 31 immediately succeeding the entry of a judgment foreclosing the property under this section, or in a contested case 21 days after the entry of a judgment foreclosing the property under this section.
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78k - Michigan Legislature
note: Former owners may instead claim remaining sale proceeds by filing a notice with the foreclosing governmental unit by the July 1 after foreclosure (MCL 211.78t(2)).

answer: The deed must vest fee simple title in the highest bidder, unless the county finds a defect in the foreclosure or the sale is canceled.
quote: The deed must vest fee simple title to the property in the person bidding the highest amount above the minimum bid, unless the foreclosing governmental unit discovers a defect in the foreclosure of the property under sections 78 to 78l or the sale is canceled under this subsection or subsection (5).
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
note: Tax-Sale.info's FAQ says buyers at its Michigan auctions receive a quitclaim deed.

answer: The foreclosure judgment extinguishes all existing recorded and unrecorded interests except, among others listed in the statute, a visible or recorded easement or right-of-way, private deed restrictions, and the interest of a lessee under a recorded oil or gas lease.
quote: That all existing recorded and unrecorded interests in that property are extinguished, except a visible or recorded easement or right-of-way, private deed restrictions, interests of a lessee or an assignee of an interest of a lessee under a recorded oil or gas lease
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78k - Michigan Legislature
note: 78k(5)(c) also keeps future installments of special assessments and environmental liens; 78m(12) cancels liens for demolition, safety repairs, debris removal and sewer or water charges as of the December 31 after the sale.

answer: By the December 1 after the judgment, a list of all unsold property goes to the clerk of the city, village or township where it lies, which may object in writing to the transfer of any of it.
quote: On or before December 1 immediately succeeding the entry of judgment under section 78k, a list of all property not previously sold by the foreclosing governmental unit under this section must be transferred to the clerk of the city, village, or township in which the property is located. The city, village, or township may object in writing to the transfer of 1 or more properties.
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature

answer: Tax-Sale.info, which runs auctions for many Michigan county treasurers, says property is sold as is with no refunds and buyers must research a property before the auction.
quote: There are no refunds on property purchased at any of our auctions. All property is sold as is/where is and without warranty. It is the buyer’s responsibility to conduct research prior to the auction date and gain a full understanding of the property they intend to purchase.
source_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
note: Applies to auctions conducted through Tax-Sale.info; the Michigan Department of Treasury notes many county treasurers hired Tax-Sale.info to conduct their auctions.

answer: Property not sold at the tax-foreclosure sales and not transferred to the city, village or township stays with the foreclosing governmental unit.
quote: If property not previously sold is not transferred to the city, village, or township in which the property is located under subsection (6), the foreclosing governmental unit shall retain possession of that property.
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
note: 78m(7)(a)-(c): transfer to a land bank fast track authority, convey under section 78r, or offer the property for sale, including a subsequent sale.

source_title: Taxpayer Resources

answer: A land bank may sell property for the consideration it considers proper, fair and valuable, including for no money, for value determined by the authority.

source_title: MCL - Section 124.757 - Michigan Legislature

answer: The Oceana County Land Bank Authority's application lists phone 231-873-3980 and email treas@oceana.mi.us.
quote: Phone: 231-873-3980 Fax: 231-873-1391 or email: treas@oceana.mi.us
source_title: Oceana County Land Bank Authority Residential Property Interest Application (PDF)

answer: Download and complete the Land Bank's Application for Proposals form and review the Oceana County Land Bank Authority's priorities, policies and procedures.
quote: If you are interested in purchasing a property from the Oceana County Land Bank Authority, please download and complete the Application for Proposals form and review the Oceana County Land Bank Authority priorities, policies, and procedures .
source_title: Land Bank Authority - Oceana County Michigan

answer: The Land Bank sets the consideration in its sole discretion, considering both fair market value and its property costs (acquisition, maintenance, repair, demolition, marketing and indirect costs).
quote: In each and every transfer of real property the LBA shall require good and valuable consideration in an amount determined by the LBA in its sole discretion. The LBA will consider both the fair market value of the property and the Property Costs in its determination of the consideration for each property.
source_title: Priorities, Policies and Procedures of the Oceana County Land Bank Authority (PDF)

answer: A separate application for each parcel.
quote: Please complete a separate application for each parcel.
source_title: Oceana County Land Bank Authority Residential Property Interest Application (PDF)
note: The form also says: '*Application will NOT be processed if not completed in its entirety.*'

answer: Interested parties must first submit the Calhoun County Land Bank Authority's Property Statement of Interest form.
quote: To apply, interested parties must first submit a Property Statement of Interest form.
source_title: Side Lot | Calhoun County Land Bank Authority

answer: For a side lot: the Side Lot Program Application, the CCLBA Applicant Certification Form and all required attachments; incomplete applications are denied.
quote: To apply for a residential side lot, please submit the Side Lot Program Application, CCLBA Applicant Certification Form, and all required attachments to the CCLBA. Complete applications will be processed as soon as possible, typically within 30 days. Incomplete applications will be denied.
source_title: Side Lot | Calhoun County Land Bank Authority

answer: You can submit an application for properties the Saginaw County Land Bank owns, including ones not on its sale list, but it is not required to sell all properties it owns and may withhold properties from sale.
quote: You can submit an application for other properties the Land Bank owns, but there may be a reason it was not listed for sale. The Land Bank is not required to sell all properties it owns, and may withhold properties from sale at the Land Bank manager’s discretion.
source_title: County of Saginaw, MI - Land Bank

answer: The Detroit Land Bank Authority's FAQ gives 313-974-6869 for purchase inquiries about lots it owns.
quote: If we do own the lot and it isn’t available for sale, give us a call at 313-974-6869
source_title: FAQ - English
note: The Wayne County Land Bank is a separate seller (waynecountylandbank.com, (313) 967-3669); the Wayne County Treasurer is the foreclosing governmental unit.

answer: For a Detroit Land Bank Authority side lot, make an account on the DLBA website and apply for the lot.
quote: You must make an account on the DLBA website and apply for your desired lot before attending these events.
source_title: FAQ - English
note: Wayne County Land Bank FAQ: 'You must create an account to apply for a property on the WCLB website.'

answer: The DLBA sells Side Lots for $100 each, or $250 if the lot has a structure on it.
quote: The DLBA sells Side Lots for $100 each. If the lot has a structure on it (garage, shed, gazebo, or similar), the DLBA will sell the lot for $250.
source_title: FAQ - English

answer: For side lots the DLBA accepts credit cards or money orders.
quote: The DLBA accepts payments in the form of credit cards or money orders.
source_title: FAQ - English

answer: Besides the remaining sale price, the DLBA tells buyers to be prepared for estimated closing costs including $600 closing/title fees, a $30 recording fee and a $25 tax certification fee.
quote: In addition to paying the remaining sale price on your property, you should be prepared to pay the following estimated closing costs: Closing/Title fees: $600 Recording fee: $30 Tax certification fee: $25
source_title: FAQ - English

answer: Corporations, organizations and LLCs buying a DLBA house are asked to submit a Certificate of Good Standing, proof of incorporation/organization in Michigan, and a list of board members/partners with contact information.
